$comment: Expected outcomes per fixture, defined by the standard and independent of any engine. An engine claiming Causeway conformance runs these and matches them exactly.
$evaluated_at: Fixtures are evaluated as though today were this date. Without it the date-sensitive fixtures would change verdict as they age, and a conformance suite that drifts is worse than none. An engine MUST accept an evaluation date rather than reading the wall clock, which is also what makes a receipt reproducible.

scope.$comment: The Phase 1 vertical slice. These five were chosen to cover every input class the slice needs — repo-lock, repo-decisions, repo-manifests, system-record and repo-tree — rather than to be representative. Fixtures for the remaining 22 checks land as those checks are implemented; a fixture with nothing executing it is an untested assertion.

$exit_code_precedence: When a run triggers more than one code, the leftmost wins. 4 outranks everything because a run that could not be configured or executed has not evaluated anything, and its other results are not trustworthy enough to report.

fixtures.description: A mission-tier C2 system with everything the slice checks in order. The baseline: any deviation in a later fixture is the only thing that fixture is testing.
The ADR closing SA-5.16 carries a role but no person. A † row closes on a name; a role is what the row already knew.
A pinned standard 581 days old. standard-currency is advisory at every profile, so this files a finding and the build continues — an engine that blocks here has promoted a check the standard has not.
A lock predating standard 1.3.0, with no released= line. The check cannot measure age and must say so — reporting it as pass would make every pre-1.3.0 project silently current.
A manifest with a caret range and no committed lockfile. Two independent violations of the same check; either alone fails it.
No ignore-scripts config, no --ignore-scripts on the CI invocation, and a curl-pipe-shell bootstrap. Not waiverable at any profile.

composition-state set to `greenfield`, the value SA-3.13 carried before ADR 0008. The regression fixture for the vocabulary reconciliation: an engine still accepting the retired answer set passes this, and that is the failure.

An ADR that is not decodable as UTF-8. The check cannot read the decisions directory reliably, so it must report `error` and block — this is the fixture that fails an engine which reduces exceptions to warnings.

must_not.$comment: Stated as a prohibition rather than only as an expectation because every wrong answer here is a build that went green on a check that never ran.

fixtures.description: Three † rows closed by ADRs numbered 0008, 0009 and 0010 — identifiers that straddle the point where a leading-zero token stops meaning what it looks like. Everything here passes; the fixture exists so that an engine which mis-reads the identifiers reports a failure the standard does not expect.
fixtures.$why: Every other fixture numbers its ADRs 0001, which is the same value under every parse. A corpus that only exercises identifiers below the first boundary cannot detect an engine that breaks at one: 0008 and 0009 are where a naive octal read fails and falls back to a string, and 0010 is where it silently succeeds with the wrong value. All three sit in one directory so a collision between a mis-parsed 0010 and the literal 0008 is observable rather than latent. The standard shipped exactly this bug in its own decision record for seven releases; see ADR 0017.
